headline_en: Trust in '999' restored: over 25 million emergency services in 7 years
summary_en: Feature on Bangladesh's national emergency number 999, its call volumes since 2017 and its collapse and recovery after 5 August 2024. Among example cases, 999 helped a Saudi Arabia-bound migrant, Momin Sheikh, recover a bag holding his passport and air ticket that fell from a train on 27 March, so he could catch his flight. 999 officials say it handles trafficking among other emergencies and is free from any phone.

facts.statement: Bangladesh's National Emergency Service number is 999; anyone anywhere in the country can call it free of charge from any phone; it runs under the Ministry of Home Affairs and links police, fire service and ambulance/health services.

999 was launched on 12 December 2017; according to 999 Police Inspector Anwar Sattar it is used for emergency help in accidents, saving human and animal lives, wildlife rescue, stopping child marriage, fires, lost items, trafficking (pachar) and violence. bKash-related fraud and family land disputes are not emergencies but people still call 999 about them.
facts.source_in_article: Anwar Sattar, Police Inspector, 999 media and public relations section

facts.statement: On 27 March, Saudi Arabia-based migrant Momin Sheikh (45), of the railway colony in Sirajganj Sadar, was standing at the door of the Dhumketu Express from Bangabandhu Bridge East station to Dhaka when his bag with his passport and air ticket fell out of the train. A fellow passenger, Fahim, called 999 saying that without the bag Momin could not board his 2 pm flight to Saudi Arabia that day and could lose his job if he did not join work on time.

After the 999 call about Momin Sheikh's lost passport bag, 999 informed the railway police control room and the Tangail railway police outpost (fari); the outpost found that a woman, Hajera Begum (40), had the bag; she brought it to the Tangail railway police outpost and it was handed back to Momin Sheikh.

From 1 January to 31 October 2024, 999 received 6,635,312 calls; 3,354,497 were given service (50.56%); the remaining 3,280,815 were outside emergency scope and the callers were advised to contact the relevant department.

From launch on 12 December 2017 to 31 October 2024, 999 received 58,488,107 calls, of which 25,350,388 were given service (43.34%); 33,137,719 callers (56.66%) were advised to contact the relevant department. Over seven years 1,933,294 calls sought emergency service: police served 1,606,240, fire service 156,129 and ambulance 170,925.
From 5 August to 15 November 2024, 999 received 2,159,281 calls; 999 currently gets on average 22,000 calls a day and on 29 July 2024 received 48,000 calls; it can take 80 calls at once.

After the fall of the Sheikh Hasina government on 5 August 2024, the police-dependent 999 service collapsed because most police were away from work and most calls could not be received; normal service resumed after police returned to stations under the interim government.

headline_en: Bangladeshi students in the US at all-time record, up 26 percent, ranking up 6 places
summary_en: The 2024 Open Doors Report shows over 17,000 Bangladeshi students in US higher education in 2023-24, up 26 percent, moving Bangladesh from 13th to 8th among sending countries. The article gives overall international student numbers and says the US Embassy in Dhaka is holding International Education Week sessions, with a contact email for EducationUSA.

facts.statement: According to the 2024 Open Doors Report on International Educational Exchange, more than 17,000 Bangladeshi students (17,099 in 2023-24) are studying at US higher education institutions, a 26 percent rise over the previous academic year (given as 2022-2023); Bangladesh rose from 13th to 8th place among countries sending international students to the US within one year.
The number of Bangladeshi students in the US rose 250 percent in a decade, from 4,802 in 2013-14 to 17,099 in 2023-24.

The Open Doors Report is published every year by the US State Department's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs and the Institute of International Education, covering international student enrolment at US universities and pre-academic intensive English programmes.

International students in the US reached a record 1,126,690 in 2023-24, 7 percent more than the year before; undergraduate students rose 8 percent to 502,291; participation in graduate-level practical work experience programmes rose 22 percent; community college enrolment rose 13 percent to 59,315.
In 2023 international students contributed more than USD 50 billion to the US economy and supported over 368,000 jobs, according to the US Department of Commerce.

For International Education Week 2024 the US Embassy in Dhaka is holding virtual and in-person sessions on applying to US higher education, academic programmes, funding/scholarships and US government-sponsored exchange programmes; for more information interested people can email EducationUSA-Bangla@state.gov.

headline_en: What happened in the interim government's first 100 days
summary_en: A day-by-day timeline of events from 8 August to mid-November 2024 under the interim government. Most items are domestic politics, but a few concern migrants: the UAE pardoned 57 Bangladeshis jailed for protesting in July, Malaysia's prime minister promised to take 18,000 workers, the chief adviser opened an airport lounge for migrants, and a cheaper Hajj package was announced.

facts.statement: 57 Bangladeshis detained in the UAE for demonstrating in July 2024 in support of the anti-discrimination student movement were sentenced; on 3 September 2024 the UAE pardoned all 57 convicted Bangladeshis, out of respect for Chief Adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus.
On 4 October 2024 Malaysia's prime minister gave an assurance to take 18,000 workers (from Bangladesh).
On 11 November 2024 the chief adviser inaugurated a lounge for expatriates (probashi) at the airport.
On 30 October 2024 the Hajj package was announced and the cost was reduced.

headline_en: Who is coming to operate Chattogram's New Mooring terminal
summary_en: The article covers the process to hand Chattogram port's New Mooring Container Terminal to UAE-based DP World under a G2G public-private partnership, and arguments for and against. Sources close to the government say bilateral ties with the UAE matter partly because of manpower export, and give the UAE's remittance figure for FY2023-24.

facts.statement: In fiscal year 2023-24, remittance equal to USD 4.64 billion (464 crore US dollars) came to Bangladesh from the UAE, which is now among the top sources of remittance.
facts.source_in_article: Sources close to the government (as reported)

facts.statement: Sources close to the government say Bangladesh is giving weight to bilateral relations with the UAE in deciding on DP World operating the New Mooring Container Terminal because issues such as Bangladesh's manpower export to the UAE are also in play.

headline_en: Because of unemployment, corruption and discrimination, 55% of youth want to go abroad: research
summary_en: The British Council's 'Next Generation Bangladesh 2024' survey of 3,081 people aged 18-35, conducted in November-December 2023, found 42 percent of youth worried about unemployment and 55 percent interested in going abroad. It lists the causes young people give for unemployment and other findings on internet use, gender attitudes and education.

facts.statement: The British Council 'Next Generation Bangladesh 2024' report found that 55 percent of young Bangladeshis are interested in going abroad, which the report links to unemployment causes; 42 percent of youth are worried about unemployment. The report was released at the British Council auditorium, Fuller Road, Dhaka University, on Wednesday (6 November 2024).

The Next Generation Bangladesh 2024 survey was based on interviews with 3,081 people aged 18 to 35 from various backgrounds, conducted in November and December 2023 before the 12th parliamentary election; it was presented by Aibek Iliasov, senior research director, Evaluation and Learning, M&C Saatchi World Services. Researchers could not immediately say what share of youth wanted to go abroad in the 2015 survey.

In the survey, 37 percent of youth named corruption and nepotism as the main cause of unemployment, 20 percent discrimination in hiring, and 18 percent inability to balance family life and work; 44 percent want to start a business within the next year.

66 percent of Bangladeshi youth use the internet regularly (77 percent of young men, 56 percent of young women); education is the top area where youth want progress, with 49 percent citing poor teaching quality, especially teaching and curricula not matched to the modern job market.

headline_en: Hajj cost reduced, packages announced
summary_en: The government finalised Hajj 2025 packages on Wednesday (30 October 2024): two government packages of BDT 478,242 and BDT 575,680 and a private general package of BDT 483,156, with one package about BDT 1 lakh cheaper than 2024. The article gives the Hajj calendar, payment rules, passport validity, and a list of pilgrims' tips, including warnings against middlemen and packages priced below the announced rate.

facts.statement: Hajj may be held in Saudi Arabia on 4 June 2025, subject to moon sighting; 127,198 people from Bangladesh will be able to perform Hajj this time.

Government-managed Hajj 2025 packages: BDT 478,242 (housing within 3 km of Masjid al-Haram) and BDT 575,680 (housing within 1.5 km of Masjid al-Haram); private general package BDT 483,156. Packages were finalised at the Hajj management executive committee meeting at the Secretariat on Wednesday chaired by Religious Affairs Adviser A F M Khalid Hossain.
Hajj 2024 costs were: government general package BDT 578,840, government special package BDT 936,320, private general package BDT 589,800. One 2025 package is BDT 1 lakh cheaper than last year.
The 2024 Hajj packages were calculated at BDT 29.74 per Saudi riyal; the 2025 packages at BDT 32.50 per riyal, so the Saudi-part costs, which must be paid in riyal, will rise for pilgrims.
Hajj 2025 timeline: Hajj agreement with the Saudi government on 13 January 2025; Hajj visas start 19 February 2025; Hajj flights start 29 April 2025.

The full Hajj package money must be paid only into the bank account of the relevant Hajj agency or directly at the agency, and pilgrims must keep the payment receipt; no dealings with middlemen are allowed; women and children must deposit money together with their mahram.
Each pilgrim must pay the sacrifice (qurbani) cost of 1,000 riyal separately; one package provides housing 1.5 km from the outer boundary of the Haram, the other 3 km.
For Hajj 2025, people aged 65 or above can go; pilgrims' passports must be valid until 31 December 2025; those without a passport should make one now matching their national ID card.

Experienced pilgrims advise: check the package length, how long you stay in Saudi Arabia and where; find out under which moallem number the agency has operated in recent years (there are moallems numbered 1 to 115 for South Asian countries, and the distance from Jamarat to the Mina tent depends on the moallem cluster price); get in writing what extra services the moallem gives for extra charges, as this causes disputes in Mina.

Pilgrims are advised to check the type of housing in Makkah and Madinah, its distance from the Kaaba, whether it has a lift, how many share a room and bathroom, whether three meals are given, whether there is a 'fitra' (shifting of house in Makkah) before or after Hajj, and arrangements for food and transport at Mina and Arafat.

To avoid fraud over the sacrifice (qurbani), it is better to buy an Islamic Development Bank (IDB) coupon; otherwise know in advance how you will be sure the sacrifice is done if you or the agency's person buys a goat.

Going on Hajj for less money than the announced package carries a risk of being cheated; never sign an agreement with a middleman, broker (dalal) or so-called moallem; check which agencies have complaints from the Saudi Hajj Ministry.
If possible make your passport yourself; if someone else makes it for you, check that your name and address in the passport are correct.

Prothom Alo has for 16 years published a free Hajj guide, available at www.prothomalo.com/widgets/hajj-guide/hajj_guide.pdf and from Prothom Alo offices in Dhaka and elsewhere; Hajj news is at www.prothomalo.com/religion/islam.

headline_en: Dr Yunus urges Saudi Arabia to invest more in Bangladesh
summary_en: On Monday 28 October 2024 Chief Adviser Yunus met Saudi Ambassador Essa Yousef Essa Al-Duhailan and asked Saudi Arabia to invest, including in training Bangladeshi youth so more skilled workers can go to Saudi Arabia. The ambassador said skill upgrading would raise migrants' pay and remittances. About 3 million Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Essa Yousef Essa Al-Duhailan said that if the skills of Bangladeshi expatriates are raised, they will earn higher wages and be able to send much more remittance home.

headline_en: Body of Saudi migrant who killed himself on video call with wife and two children arrives after 22 days
summary_en: Khokon Howlader, from Mirzaganj, Patuakhali, who had lived in Saudi Arabia for seven or eight years, hanged himself on 24 September while on a video call with his twin sons and wife. His body arrived at Dhaka airport on a Biman flight 22 days later (16 October 2024) and was buried at home on 17 October.

facts.statement: Saudi Arabia-based Bangladeshi migrant Khokon Howlader hanged himself from a ceiling fan with a gamchha-like cloth on 24 September while on a mobile video call with his twin sons Abdul Karim Shanto and Abdur Rahim Shaon and his wife Nupur Begum; he had lived in Saudi Arabia for seven to eight years.

Khokon Howlader's body arrived 22 days after his death, at 4 pm on Wednesday (16 October 2024) on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka; it was taken by hearse to West Subidkhali, Deuli Subidkhali union, Mirzaganj upazila, Patuakhali, arriving about 2 am, and buried after janaza at 9 am on Thursday (17 October 2024).
facts.source_in_article: Reporter / UP member Md Atikur Rahman

facts.statement: Relatives say Khokon Howlader had recently come home on leave and returned to his workplace in Saudi Arabia on 14 October; the article prints this date even though it gives his death as 24 September, so the dates conflict.

headline_en: 'Everything is finished for me': three Munshiganj workers die after Malaysia factory blast
summary_en: An explosion at a chemical factory in Malaysia on Thursday (10 October 2024) burned three Bangladeshi workers from the same village in Munshiganj, all of whom died. Abdus Salam (24) had gone to Malaysia 1.5 years earlier on BDT 3.5 lakh borrowed at interest, through his maternal uncle Abu Taher, and his mother still owes BDT 2 lakh. Families want the bodies brought home quickly; the Munshiganj DC says contact with the Bangladesh High Commission in Malaysia is ongoing.

facts.statement: At about 11:30 am on Thursday (10 October 2024) an explosion at a chemical factory in Malaysia burned three Bangladeshi workers over most of their bodies: Abdus Salam (24), his maternal uncle Abu Taher (32) and Jabbar Ali (42), all from Ramzanbeg area, Munshiganj municipality. Jabbar Ali died on Friday (11 October), Abu Taher at dawn on Saturday (12 October) and Salam at about 5 pm on Sunday (13 October) while under treatment.
Jabbar Ali's nephew Khairul Islam said the three burned workers lay on the road for an hour and a half after the blast and that some might have survived if treatment had started in time.
facts.source_in_article: Khairul Islam, nephew of Jabbar Ali

facts.statement: Abdus Salam's mother Taslima Begum said she borrowed BDT 3.5 lakh at interest from various people to send Salam to Malaysia about 1.5 years earlier through her brother Abu Taher; Salam could not work for the first six months and sent some money within a year; she has repaid BDT 1.5 lakh including interest and still owes lenders BDT 2 lakh.
Abu Taher had gone to Malaysia 10 years earlier and worked for the same company for 10 years; because the company was good, he took his nephew Salam there 1.5 years ago.

Munshiganj Deputy Commissioner Fatema Tul Jannat said on 14 October 2024 that contact is ongoing with the Bangladesh High Commission in Malaysia on how to bring the bodies home quickly, and that the administration is checking on the victims' families. Families demanded the government bring the bodies quickly.

headline_en: Why are Middle East-based remittance fighters third class: on colonial domination
summary_en: Opinion piece by Shahida Khanam arguing that low-skilled migrant workers going to the Middle East, Malaysia and Singapore are treated with colonial contempt at Bangladeshi airports, while professionals going West are treated with deference. She describes officials filling forms for money, abusive shouting at passport queues and luggage being slit and goods stolen.

facts.statement: The writer says that at the airport a class of officials fill in the checking (embarkation) form for low-skilled, often illiterate migrant workers in exchange for money.

The writer says migrant workers returning on leave are shouted at in obscene language in passport-check lines and that their bags are cut open and goods stolen; returning migrants usually bring foreign blankets, gold and electronics.
The writer says the current government has announced it will arrange a separate venue (area) for migrant workers at the airport.
The writer says skilled professionals (academics, engineers, doctors) going to Europe, America, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are only 4 percent of total migration.

headline_en: Germany's Opportunity Card: students, learn the application process and details
summary_en: Explainer (source: UNB) on Germany's Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte), a residence permit of up to one year for non-EU skilled people to look for work. It sets out the two eligibility routes, the points system (minimum 6 points), benefits, the VIDEX online application, the documents list, the EUR 75 fee at the German Embassy in Dhaka, and processing time of a few weeks to six months.

facts.statement: Germany's Opportunity Card is a residence permit for skilled workers from outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland to enter Germany to look for a job; it is valid for at most one year, within which the holder must find employment, and the applicant must give proof of qualifications for the relevant work.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Opportunity Card route 1: people with professional or academic qualifications fully recognised by Germany, obtained in Germany or from a Germany-recognised institution in their home country.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Opportunity Card route 2 (not yet established skilled workers) requires: an academic degree from a German university or a Germany-recognised university at home, or at least two years of vocational training from a German or Germany-recognised institution; plus German at least CEFR A1 or English at least CEFR B2. The article says IELTS 5.5 to 6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72 to 94 are equivalent to CEFR B2.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Route 2 applicants are scored on points; those with at least 6 points have a better chance of getting the card. Partial recognition of degree/training: 4 points (also given for licensable professions before licensing, but the licence exam must be passed before the residence permit). Qualification in a shortage occupation: 1 point (e.g. mining manager, health service manager, chemist, civil engineer, graphic and multimedia designer, software developer).
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Opportunity Card points continued: work experience after the degree of at least 2 years within the last 5 years = 2 points, at least 5 years within the last 7 years = 3 points; German A2 = 1 point, B1 (printed as 'B1-A2') and B2 or above = 3 points, plus 1 extra point for English C1 or above or native speaker; age under 35 = 2 points, 35 to 40 = 1 point; at least six months' legal stay in Germany within the last five years (visit, study or work) = 1 point; if one spouse meets the Opportunity Card conditions, the other gets 1 point.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: The Opportunity Card initially allows up to one year in Germany to look for work; after one year the holder can apply from within Germany to extend it up to two years; holders may seek a job or self-employment, work part-time up to a total of 20 hours a week in one or more jobs, and do job trials of up to two weeks per company.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Application steps: first book an appointment through the online appointment system; then complete the online application on the VIDEX portal; print the completed application and sign it yourself; after booking you get a confirmation email with the date; on that date go to the German Embassy with the application and all documents.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Documents for the Opportunity Card visa include: completed VIDEX form; valid passport issued within the last 10 years with at least two blank pages, plus copies of data page and previous visas; one recent biometric passport photo (not older than six months); signed declaration of consent (https://dhaka.diplo.de/bd-en/service/visa-einreise/-/2669542); vocational or academic certificates with German recognition of equivalence (original plus copy); licence to practise for licensable professions (e.g. medical licence); experience confirmation letters from previous employers.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo scholarship section, citing UNB

facts.statement: Further documents: motivation letter or statement of purpose covering the kind of work sought in Germany, the period of German study, why Germany among EU countries, companies applied to or interviews, CV and cover letter (in English and also German), proof of funds via a blocked account in Germany of at least EUR 1,027 per month, sufficient funds for a return flight, and an original declaration of commitment if someone else bears the costs; proof of health insurance (travel health insurance for the first three weeks plus a letter from a German health provider, or public German health insurance); proof of accommodation in Germany (written invitation from a host family or hotel booking with full address); for previous legal stay in Germany: rental contract, employment terms, service contract, passport with visas and entry stamps; spouses applying together should attach the marriage certificate.

headline_en: Anwar Ibrahim pledges steps to take 18,000 workers
summary_en: On a Friday visit to Dhaka (4 October 2024), Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said his government would immediately attend to the entry of 18,000 Bangladeshi workers in the first phase, subject to all conditions being met, and that workers must not be treated as modern slaves. He also asked Bangladesh not to shelter criminal activity by Bangladeshis in Malaysia. About 800,000 Bangladeshis work in Malaysia.

facts.statement: At a joint press conference with Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus at a Dhaka hotel (InterContinental) on a Friday (about 4 October 2024), Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said his government would immediately give attention to the going of 18,000 Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia in the first phase, subject to all conditions being met, while ensuring a proper working environment.

Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia needs workers and they cannot be treated as modern slaves, wherever they come from; he also urged Bangladesh to be cautious and not to indulge criminal activities by any Bangladeshi or foreigner living in Malaysia.
About 800,000 (8 lakh) Bangladeshis currently work in Malaysia; about 450,000 (sare char lakh) of them migrated between August 2022 and May 2024.

Anwar Ibrahim stressed quick resolution of problems faced by Malaysian companies in Bangladesh and Bangladeshi companies in Malaysia and said a Joint Commission meeting could be held as soon as possible; it was the first visit to Bangladesh by a Malaysian prime minister in about a decade.

headline_en: Kafil and Soma receive Abu Khaled Pathan literary award
No one declared homes or cars abroad in tax files
summary_en: No Bangladeshi taxpayer has declared foreign assets in tax returns since NBR allowed it in 2022, despite reports of politicians' and businesspeople's assets abroad. The article explains the 10(B) asset statement form and why taxpayers avoid declaring, and notes that 3,604 Bangladeshis have settled in Malaysia under its Second Home programme.

facts.statement: Bangladesh's National Board of Revenue (NBR) first allowed declaring foreign assets in income tax files in the 2022 budget; no taxpayer has done so. The same budget allowed bringing back laundered money for one year by paying a set tax rate with no questions asked; no one used it.

In the annual tax return a taxpayer gives income, expenditure and asset information; the asset statement is filed on form 10(B), which is mandatory if assets at home and abroad exceed BDT 50 lakh; column 9 of form 10(B) is for assets held abroad. Bangladesh has more than 10 million TIN holders, of whom more than 3.5 million file returns.

Tax officials say taxpayers avoid declaring foreign assets because of possible double taxation, because assets bought with laundered money could be caught by agencies such as the Anti-Corruption Commission and Bangladesh Bank, and because assets from income earned abroad are safer to show in the foreign tax file and there is no obligation to show them in the Bangladeshi tax file.
So far 3,604 Bangladeshis have settled in Malaysia under the Malaysia 'Second Home' programme; many Bangladeshi businesspeople have also settled in Canada and Singapore through investment programmes.

headline_en: Many Awami League leaders have left the country
summary_en: After the fall of the Sheikh Hasina government, many Awami League leaders and ex-ministers left Bangladesh illegally across the border into India, paying brokers on both sides. The article names border areas used, prices (BDT 50,000 to 25-30 lakh per person), a retired judge robbed by those helping him, and a death at the border.

facts.statement: Families and associates of people who fled say illegal exits to India after 5 August 2024 went mostly through Sylhet, Akhaura (Brahmanbaria), Netrokona and Mymensingh (Haluaghat), the Jashore region, Lalmonirhat and other northern border areas; each person paid brokers (dalal) on both sides of the border from BDT 50,000 up to BDT 25-30 lakh.
facts.source_in_article: Families, colleagues of those who left

facts.statement: Retired Appellate Division justice Shamsuddin Chowdhury (Manik) was caught by locals at the Kanaighat border, Sylhet, on 23 August 2024 while fleeing to India; in a video he said he had a BDT 15,000 deal to cross, and that those helping him took the BDT 60-70 lakh he carried and beat him on the other side of the border.

Former Chhatra League general secretary Ishaque Ali Khan (Panna) died on the night of 24 August 2024 while crossing to India through the Dona border at Kanaighat, Sylhet; Meghalaya police said he died of strangulation.

Sources say some people who entered India illegally are using brokers to get Bangladesh exit and Indian entry stamps put in their passports; some are trying to 'manage' Indian immigration to move to other countries, and the former Sylhet mayor Anwaruzzaman Chowdhury is reported to have gone from India to London this way.
Former Additional IGP Naim Ahmed said checkpoints and surveillance should be strengthened and action taken against people involved in human trafficking at the border.
